questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Ahuja is a __cleverest__ lawyer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the superlative form "**cleverest**" with the article "**a**".
 
• Superlative adjectives are used with the definite article "**the**."
 
• Using "**a cleverest**" is grammatically incorrect because it mixes an indefinite article with a superlative adjective.
 
• Since no comparison is being made among all lawyers, the correct form should simply be "**a clever lawyer**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1: clever**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Ahuja is a clever lawyer."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative degree** (e.g., cleverer/more clever) is used when comparing two entities.
 
• **Superlative degree** (e.g., cleverest/most clever) is used when comparing more than two entities and should be preceded by "**the**".
 
• When no comparison is involved, the **positive degree** ("clever") is used with the indefinite article "a."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Curse
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 (Praise)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Curse"** refers to an expression of a wish that misfortune, evil, or harm happens to someone or something. It can also mean words spoken in anger intended to bring bad luck. (शाप देना / अपशब्द कहना)

 
 
• **Example:** The old woman put a curse on the village after being banished.
 
 
 
• **"Praise"** refers to an expression of approval, admiration, or respect for someone or something. It is the opposite of curse as it conveys positive feelings rather than negative ones. (प्रशंसा करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher praised the student for their excellent performance in the exam.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the antonym of **"Curse"** is **"Praise"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 (Praise)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Criticise** (आलोचना करना): To express disapproval of someone or something by pointing out flaws or mistakes.

 
 
• **Example:** The article criticised the government’s policies for being ineffective.
 
 
 
• **Abuse** (गाली देना / दुर्व्यवहार करना): To use harsh or insulting language or to treat someone cruelly.
 
 
• **Example:** The manager was accused of abusing his employees verbally.
 
 
 
• **Comment** (टिप्पणी करना): To express an opinion or remark about something.
 
 
• **Example:** She made a thoughtful comment about the social issues discussed in the debate.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

She always wears dresses of ________ fashion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**the latest**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**the latest fashion**" is a fixed collocation used to refer to the most recent trends or styles.
 
• The definite article "**the**" is necessary because we are referring to a specific, identifiable trend — the most recent one.
 
• Using just "**latest**" without "**the**" would be grammatically incomplete and awkward in this context.
 
• Options like "**late**" or "**the latter**" are not appropriate adjectives to describe fashion trends.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"She always wears dresses of **the latest**__ fashion."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Latest** means “newest” or “most recent,” and when referring to trends or fashion, it typically takes the definite article "**the**".
 
• Example: "This store always sells clothes in **the latest fashion**."
 
• "**Late**" refers to time and is not used to describe fashion. "**The latter**" is used in comparisons and not suitable here.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The discussion led by the scientist was very ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**informative**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**informative**" is an adjective that describes something that provides useful or interesting information.
 
• The adverb "**very**" is used to modify adjectives in their base form, not their comparative or superlative forms.
 
• Options like "**more informative**" and "**most informative**" are incorrect here because they are not preceded by appropriate comparative structures (e.g., "than" or a list for comparison).
 
• "**Information**" is a noun, and using it directly after "very" would be grammatically incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The discussion led by the scientist was very **informative**__."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Use "**informative**" when describing events, lectures, or discussions that provide knowledge or insight.
 
• Example: "The documentary was highly informative and well-researched."
 
• The word "**very**" intensifies the adjective, and must be followed by an adjective in the correct degree.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Manisha had a great feeling for those who were __junior than__ her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adjective "**junior**" is a comparative that is always followed by the preposition "**to**", not "*than*".
 
• This rule also applies to other similar comparatives like "**senior**", "**inferior**", "**superior**", etc.
 
• Using "**than**" after "**junior**" is grammatically incorrect in standard English usage.
 
• Therefore, the phrase "**junior than her**" must be corrected to "**junior to her**".

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1: junior to**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Manisha had a great feeling for those who were junior to her."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Junior to"** is the correct grammatical construction when comparing relative rank or age.
 
• Examples: "He is junior to me in the company." / "They are senior to us by two years."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Wolves' teeth are larger and __strong__ than dog's teeth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains a comparative structure signaled by the word "**than**".
 
• In comparatives, adjectives should be in their comparative form to match the structure (e.g., "larger **and stronger**").
 
• The word "**strong**" is in its base form, which is incorrect in this context.
 
• The correct comparative form of "strong" is "**stronger**", which must be used to maintain parallelism with "larger".

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1: stronger**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Wolves' teeth are larger and stronger than dog's teeth."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When comparing two things, use the comparative degree of adjectives: "**larger, stronger, smaller, faster**", etc.
 
• The use of "**more + adjective**" is generally for adjectives with two or more syllables (e.g., more beautiful, more dangerous).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Native' from the given sentence.

Mr. Smith believes that various tribes are the indigenous habitants of various corners of the world; unlike his contemporaries who have a viewpoint regarding an alien or foreign invasion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Indigenous**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Native"** refers to someone or something that originates from a particular place or country. It often implies being born in or naturally belonging to a specific area. (मूल निवासी)

 
 
• **Example:** The kangaroo is native to Australia.
 
 
 
• **"Indigenous"** means originating or occurring naturally in a particular place; it is often used to describe the first inhabitants of a region. (स्वदेशी)
 
 
• **Example:** The indigenous tribes of the Amazon rainforest have lived there for centuries.
 
 
 
• Hence, the word "Indigenous" is the most appropriate synonym for "Native".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Indigenous**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Foreign** (विदेशी): Refers to something or someone that belongs to a different country or place.

 
 
• **Example:** She loves trying foreign cuisines when she travels.
 
 
 
• **Alien** (अजनबी): Something or someone unfamiliar or from a different world or context.
 
 
• **Example:** The customs of this new country felt alien to him.
 
 
 
• **Invasion** (आक्रमण): An aggressive entry into a place, often by force.
 
 
• **Example:** The invasion of the enemy forces was swift and unexpected.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**dominates; around**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The preposition "**around**" fits well to convey global reach and influence, aligning with the phrase "around the world."
 
• Other options such as "command; besides", "controls; beside", and "presides; round" are grammatically or contextually awkward in this sentence.
 
• Hence, "dominates" and "around" together convey both authority and worldwide popularity effectively.

**Complete Sentence:** *Michael Jackson is known as the King of Pop. He **dominates**__ his own genre of music, Pop. His music is spreading its influence and popularity __**around**__ the world.*

• **Dominates**: Means to have a commanding influence over (प्रभुत्व जमाना).
 
• **Around the world**: A standard phrase to indicate global presence or reach.
 
• Incorrect pairings like "beside" and "besides" don’t fit spatial or comparative contexts in this sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence in the present perfect continuous tense.

The company _______________ working towards achievements in curbing slackness and fostering development.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**has been**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires the use of the **present perfect continuous tense**, which is formed using "**has/have been + present participle (verb+ing)**".
 
• The subject "**the company**" is singular, so the correct auxiliary verb is "**has**", not "have".
 
• Options like "**is being**" and "**are being**" form part of the present continuous passive voice, which is not suitable here.
 
• Therefore, the correct structure is "**has been working**", matching the tense and subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The company **has been**__ working towards achievements in curbing slackness and fostering development."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Continuous Tense** is used to describe an action that began in the past and is still continuing or has recently stopped.
 
• Structure: **has/have been + verb-ing** (e.g., "She has been reading," "They have been studying").
 
• Always ensure the verb form and subject-verb agreement match the tense being used.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• The verb "**shot**" is the correct choice as it precisely describes what a sharpshooter does — firing a gun or similar weapon at a target.
 
• The phrase "**shot dead**" is an established collocation used to indicate that someone has been killed by gunfire.
 
• Words like "**fixed**", "**threw**", or "**killed**" do not fit naturally in this expression, especially in the context of a sharpshooter's action.
 
• Hence, "**shot dead**" is the most appropriate and idiomatic phrase for this sentence.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The sharpshooter **shot**__ dead a man-eating tiger after it allegedly killed nine people in the last few days.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Shot dead**: A common phrase used in reports and news to refer to someone being fatally shot.
 
• **Sharpshooter**: A person who is extremely skilled at shooting targets, usually using firearms.

questions.solution:

• The correct word should be "**late**," which indicates tardiness or delay in action — suitable for time-based events like waking up late.
 
• "Unpardonably late" accurately conveys the idea of being so late that it is almost unforgivable.
 
• Therefore, the adverb "**lately**" must be replaced with the adjective "**late**" to correctly complete the phrase.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4: unpardonably lately in the morning**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He missed the college bus because he woke up unpardonably late in the morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lately** means “recently” and is used for actions that happened in the near past (e.g., "I have seen him lately").
 
• **Late** refers to being delayed or not on time and is appropriate for specific moments or schedules (e.g., "He arrived late to class").
